The bad news is the VRAM arithmetic on 32GB, and it is unforgiving:

- The bf16 drafter is 5.16 GiB of weights (lm_head and embeddings are shared with the target -- good design, they cost nothing). With a multimodal target (vision tower resident) there is simply no room left for a usable KV pool.
- Even with the 2.4 GiB quantized drafter, the best stable config we found caps the KV pool at about 40% of what the same server allocates without speculation. We swept gpu-memory-utilization and cudagraph sizes; above that point we hit a constant OOM wall during graph capture regardless of how much KV we gave back.
- And the drafter's KV has a shape worth knowing: five full-width layers with a 2048 sliding window is a near-fixed per-request cost, so it is proportionally most expensive exactly where production lives -- at 8-16k contexts it adds 34-39% KV per request, while at 131k it only adds 10%. The engine's "GPU KV cache size: N tokens" line is anchored to max_model_len, which makes the hit look much smaller than it is for short-context workloads.

So on this card the trade is +15-26% throughput against roughly half the resident concurrency at realistic context lengths, and we ended up not deploying it -- the speedup is real but the concurrency is what pays our bills. On 48GB+ none of this should bind and the PR looks like a straight win. Two things would change the picture on consumer hardware: an official quantized drafter (our RTN numbers suggest it is free quality-wise), and possibly a knob to cap the drafter's KV admission separately from the target's.

Happy to share the quantization recipe or the sweep harness if useful.

**TechPrototyper** (2026-08-22T00:13:12Z):

**Quantized DFlash2 draft checkpoints: fused-layer scale loading fails (repro included)**

First: thanks for this PR — we have been running the DFlash2 path
(cherry-picked from this PR + #52883 onto an sm121/GB10 build) against a
27B hybrid target for several days with excellent results (draft length 7,
verified quality-neutral at GSM8K n=1319 paired, McNemar p=0.12; details
in our public lab notebook¹).

One follow-on gap you may want on the radar: **quantized draft
checkpoints load only if the quantized layers are unfused.**

Repro (compressed-tensors, fp8 weights, both `per-tensor` and `channel`
strategies, `"quantization": "compressed-tensors"` set in the
speculative config):

- Quantizing only `o_proj` + `down_proj` (unfused `RowParallelLinear`):
  loads and serves cleanly; acceptance is unchanged vs. the bf16 drafter
  (5.08 vs 5.11 mean acceptance length in our runs).
- Quantizing `q/k/v_proj` or `gate/up_proj` (fused into
  `QKVParallelLinear` / `MergedColumnParallelLinear`): engine init fails
  during weight loading:

```
File ".../model_executor/layers/linear.py", line 1011, in load_weights
File ".../model_executor/layers/linear.py", line 754, in weight_loader
AttributeError: 'MergedColumnParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'data'
```

i.e. the per-shard `weight_scale` resolves to the module instead of the
parameter on the DFlash2 draft-model loading path. The scheme matching
itself works (targets resolve, unfused layers get quantized correctly),
which isolates the failure to fused-scale loading for this model class.

Happy to provide the full traceback, the checkpoint-generation script,
or to test a fix on sm121 — quantized drafters look like a natural
follow-on to this PR (the drafter is the one component where
quantization is quality-risk-free by construction under verified
sampling; only acceptance can move, and in our measurement it didn't).

¹ https://github.com/TechPrototyper/local-ai-lab/blob/master/notes/dflash2-drafter-fp8-quant.md

**jschmied** (2026-08-22T05:52:00Z):

@TechPrototyper That failure has a number: [#53116](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53116) — the draft model's quant config never reaches `packed_modules_mapping`, so the fused layers are built without a scheme and the per-shard `weight_scale` resolves to the module. Worth knowing before you get there: **a second wall sits right behind it.** Once the drafter loads, DFlash's fused context-KV precompute slices `qkv_proj.weight` raw and applies it with a bare `F.linear`, bypassing `quant_method` — so a drafter with quantized `q/k/v` dies at startup profiling with `expected mat1 and mat2 to have the same dtype`. That is [#51581](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51581); #53122 now carries a dequantize-at-buffer-build fix for it too. Your unfused-only result is consistent with exactly this: `o_proj`/`down_proj` never touch that path.

**jschmied** (2026-08-22T20:05:40Z):

@TechPrototyper Thanks — and you found a real gap, not a documentation gap. Fixed.

The dequant path handled a per-tensor scalar and a per-row vector, but not the third form your checkpoint has: a per-tensor scheme on a **fused** layer stores one scalar _per shard_, so `weight_scale` is `(3,)` for q/k/v — neither `numel()==1` nor `numel()==out_features`. It now expands each shard's scalar over the rows that shard owns, using `output_partition_sizes` (falling back to `output_sizes`), and only then slices `[q_size:]`, so K and V each get their own scale:

```python
sizes = getattr(qkv, 'output_partition_sizes', None) or getattr(
  qkv, 'output_sizes', None
)
if sizes is not None and s.numel() == len(sizes) and sum(sizes) == w.shape[0]:
  s = torch.cat([s[i].expand(int(n)) for i, n in enumerate(sizes)])
```

The `sum(sizes) == w.shape[0]` guard keeps it from firing on a coincidental length match; anything it still cannot map keeps the explicit error rather than silently broadcasting one shard's scale across another's rows — which would not crash and would only show up as worse acceptance.

Branch, on the #52816 merge commit:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/compare/b389ac29465b33f9e9c534df221ea3c129e9793f...jschmied:vllm:dflash-quantized-drafter

Verified against synthetic tensors for all four cases — per-shard `(3,)`, per-tensor scalar, per-channel full-length, and unquantized pass-through — plus the error path. Not verified against a real per-tensor fused checkpoint, since I do not have one; if your offer to test that variant still stands, that is the piece I am missing.

@Tejas-Raj01 — worth folding into #53122 alongside the part you already took.

Your numbers are a useful second data point: fp8-full 42.5 tok/s single-stream and 205.2 at c=8 against 38–42 / 179 for BF16, acceptance 5.05 vs 5.11. Same direction as ours on a different target and harness — quantizing the drafter buys throughput and costs no measurable acceptance.
